meta.kickoff: Kickoff 60 (stopped at the draw; no job)
meta.description: Kickoff 60, the check at the peak phase on ibm_fez, stopped at the draw: the rule's chain procedure, run once, live, at 14:01:20 UTC on 15 October 2026 on the stamp of 13:39:11 UTC, left no chain (no redraw is allowed), so no job was built on chains, no go was asked and nothing was submitted. Kept: the draw, the published values it screened on, the published readout over the previous 48 hours, the timing record and the stamp read at the draw. The rule is published beside it as a rule that refused to draw.

built_from.how: the draw by hw_60.py (draw_chains) on the live target; no circuit was built on a chain

fixed_before_the_data.if_fewer_than_four_survive: stop and report; there is no redraw (k60-rule.md)

chain_draw.procedure: k60-rule.md: candidates on the live target's CZ edges (either direction), L1 != L3; exclusions (a qubit used on ibm_fez in Kickoffs 47 to 54; operational; readout error above 3%; CZ error above 1%, the larger of the edge's listed directions; a missing value excludes); sort by (M, L1, L3); numpy.random.default_rng(6060).shuffle; take in order, skipping any chain that shares a qubit with one taken, until four

published_at_draw.what: IBM's published values at the stamp the draw screened on (13:39:11 UTC on 15 October 2026), for every qubit, from the snapshot at that stamp: readout error, P(0|1), P(1|0), T1 and T2. The snapshot is not in this repository

published_readout_over_48h.what: per published stamp over the 48 hours before the draw, from the walk's saved snapshots (readout_stamps_60.py): the median published readout error over the 156 qubits and how many lie above 3% and above 10%; and at the draw's stamp, the qubits at or below 3%

window.rule: k55-rule.md, 'When': the job is not submitted inside the window from 30 minutes before the next expected T1 stamp to 30 minutes after the next expected CZ stamp; each expected stamp is the last one plus the mean of the day-to-day intervals seen; if the 48 hours show no such pattern, no window applies
window.walk_code: history 01's walk_history.py, byte-identical, with BACKEND, INSTANCE, START, HERE and SNAP set before main()

window.note: a day-to-day interval lies outside 20 to 30 hours (k60-rule.md); the computed window does not apply; it is kept beside under computed_window_not_applied

computed_window_not_applied.note: from 30 minutes before the next expected T1 stamp to 30 minutes after the next expected CZ stamp

interval_condition.rule: k60-rule.md: if the 48 hours show no such pattern, or the day-to-day interval lies outside 20 to 30 hours, record that, and the computed window does not apply

cycle.rule: k60-rule.md: in every case, neither job is submitted while the current day's cycle is in progress: from a stamp at which T1 changed on more than half the qubits until 30 minutes after the next stamp at which CZ errors changed on more than half the edges

"""Kickoff 60 analysis, fixed before the data (sections 3 and 4 of the kickoff; k60-rule.md).

Kickoff 57's analysis through Kickoff 59's wrapper, both unchanged: analyse_59.py and analyse_57.py (byte-identical
copies). analyse_59 sets the two seeds to 59 when it is imported; they are set here to 60 as k60-rule.md fixes them
(analyse_57.SEED, the joint generator for the list beside the verdict, and analyse_53.SEED, the verdict's bootstrap
inside analyse_53.analyse), before any call. Everything else is analyse_57's:
- the peak phase from job 1 (analyse_57.peaks: OLS of M's P(1) over the six phases, theta_R1 = atan2(s, -b),
  phi* = 180 - theta_R1 wrapped to [0, 360) and rounded to the nearest whole degree, from the point estimate);
- the verdict on the four phi* cells by analyse_53.analyse (unchanged), seed 60, 10,000 draws, the copies drawn with
  replacement and each drawn copy's shots redrawn, phi* held fixed;
- beside it, from one generator (seed 60) that first repeats analyse_53's verdict draws and must equal them exactly:
  the check at +90 on the same chains, the original rule at phi* and at +90, job 1's fits with intervals, the drift;
- analyse_59's addition: each waiting qubit's zero-wait baseline P(1) (Z), with its interval from the verdict's
  bootstrap, and whether it exceeds 0.1.
The verdict key analyse_59 names H59 is reported as H60.

Added here, beside the verdict (k60-rule.md, item 1): each waiting qubit's readout from job 2's two readout circuits on
M alone, P(1|0) (P10: measure with no gate) and P(0|1) (P01: X, then measure), pooled over the two copies, with each
copy's value; beside them the published readout error, prob_meas1_prep0 and prob_meas0_prep1 of M at the stamp in force
when job 2 ran (the latest stamp read at or before IBM's running timestamp, from walk-60/ and stamps-60/) and at job 2's
submission. No interval is drawn for them (the rule fixes none, and analyse_57's generator is internal to it); the two
copies are shown instead. The readout circuits do not enter the verdict or the generator: analyse_57 passes only the
phi* circuits, W-ref and Z to analyse_53, and draws only the keys it names.

H60: DISAGREE if any informative cell's d1 interval lies entirely outside [-0.15, +0.15]; AGREE if every informative
cell's lies entirely inside; NOT SETTLED otherwise; ", uninformative" if no cell is informative.

Usage: python analyse_60.py                 (Kickoff 60's files)
       python analyse_60.py --synthetic     (analyse_57's synthetic tests at seed 60; then job 2 with the readout
                                             circuits added, built to AGREE and to DISAGREE)"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import math
import sys
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "site"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "src-e45f15d" / "tests"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import analyse_59 as A59  # noqa: E402  Kickoff 59's wrapper, unchanged (it sets the seeds to 59 on import)
A57 = A59.A57             # Kickoff 57's analysis, unchanged

A57.SEED = 60           # the joint generator beside the verdict (k60-rule.md)
A57.A53.SEED = 60       # the verdict's bootstrap (k60-rule.md)
READOUT = ("P10", "P01")


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def readout(labels2, counts2, order):
    """P(1|0) from P10 and P(0|1) from P01, per M, pooled over the copies, with each copy's value."""
    ones = defaultdict(list)
    for lab, cts in zip(labels2, counts2):
        if lab["circuit"] in READOUT:
            o, t = A57.m_ones(lab, cts)
            ones[(str(lab["M"]), lab["circuit"])].append((lab["copy"], o, t))
    out = {}
    for M in order:
        p10 = sorted(ones[(M, "P10")])
        p01 = sorted(ones[(M, "P01")])
        out[M] = {"P1_given_0": sum(x[1] for x in p10) / sum(x[2] for x in p10),
                  "P1_given_0_by_copy": [x[1] / x[2] for x in p10],
                  "P0_given_1": 1 - sum(x[1] for x in p01) / sum(x[2] for x in p01),
                  "P0_given_1_by_copy": [1 - x[1] / x[2] for x in p01],
                  "shots": {"P10": [x[2] for x in p10], "P01": [x[2] for x in p01]}}
        out[M]["mean_of_the_two"] = (out[M]["P1_given_0"] + out[M]["P0_given_1"]) / 2
    return out


def analyse(labels1, counts1, labels2, counts2, order, phistar):
    r = A59.analyse(labels1, counts1, labels2, counts2, order, phistar)
    r["H60"] = r.pop("H59")
    r["readout_measured"] = readout(labels2, counts2, order)
    return r


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the published readout beside
def _stamp_of(path):
    return datetime.strptime(path.name[len("snapshot-"):-len(".json")], "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ").replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def published_at(t, order):
    snaps = {}
    for d in (HERE / "walk-60" / "snapshots", HERE / "stamps-60"):
        for p in d.glob("snapshot-*.json") if d.exists() else []:
            snaps.setdefault(_stamp_of(p), p)
    before = [s for s in snaps if s <= t]
    if not before:
        return None
    s = max(before)
    d = json.loads(snaps[s].read_text())
    out = {"stamp_utc": s.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), "snapshot": snaps[s].parent.name + "/" + snaps[s].name, "M": {}}
    for M in order:
        q = {p["name"]: p["value"] for p in d["qubits"][int(M)]}
        out["M"][M] = {k: q.get(k) for k in ("readout_error", "prob_meas1_prep0", "prob_meas0_prep1")}
    return out


def ts(s):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(str(s).replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone(timezone.utc)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- synthetic counts with the readout circuits
def synthetic_readout():
    """analyse_57's job 2 construction (the same model and stated offsets), with the two readout circuits added per chain
    at stated P(1|0) and P(0|1); built to AGREE and to DISAGREE; the analysis must return each and recover the readout."""
    W = A57.W
    ik = sorted(W.wait_test_ideal())
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    s2 = lambda x: math.sin(math.radians(x) / 2) ** 2

    def w_counts(f, n):
        p = {k: f / 32 for k in ik}
        p["000001"] = 1 - f
        ks = list(p)
        x = rng.multinomial(n, [p[k] for k in ks])
        return {k: int(v) for k, v in zip(ks, x) if v}

    def r_counts(p1, n, bits=6):
        o = int(rng.binomial(n, min(max(p1, 0.0), 1.0)))
        if bits == 1:
            return {"0": n - o, "1": o}
        return {"0" * bits: n - o, "1" + "0" * (bits - 1): o}

    order = ["11", "22", "33", "44"]
    thR = {"11": 10, "22": -40, "33": 100, "44": -150}
    ro = {"11": (0.01, 0.02), "22": (0.03, 0.05), "33": (0.10, 0.20), "44": (0.005, 0.01)}
    ok = True
    for name, extra in (("AGREE", {}), ("DISAGREE", {"33": 90})):
        l1, c1, l2, c2 = [], [], [], []
        for M in order:
            for cp in (1, 2):
                for p in A57.PHIS1:
                    l1.append({"job": 1, "M": int(M), "circuit": "R1", "role": "sweep", "phi_deg": p, "copy": cp, "m_clbit": 5, "part": "S"})
                    c1.append(r_counts(0.01 + 0.9 * s2(p + thR[M]), 2000))
        ps = {M: v["phi_star_deg"] for M, v in A57.peaks(l1, c1, order).items()}
        for M in order:
            tW = thR[M] + extra.get(M, 0)
            for cp in (1, 2):
                for role, p, n in (("peak", ps[M], 3000), ("plus90", 90, 1500)):
                    l2.append({"job": 2, "M": int(M), "circuit": "W-no", "role": role, "phi_deg": p, "copy": cp, "part": "W"})
                    c2.append(w_counts(0.9 * (1 - 0.9 * s2(p + tW)), n))
                    l2.append({"job": 2, "M": int(M), "circuit": "R1", "role": role, "phi_deg": p, "copy": cp, "m_clbit": 5, "part": "R"})
                    c2.append(r_counts(0.01 + 0.9 * s2(p + thR[M]), n))
                    l2.append({"job": 2, "M": int(M), "circuit": "R0", "role": role, "phi_deg": p, "copy": cp, "m_clbit": 0, "part": "R"})
                    c2.append(r_counts(0.01 + 0.9 * s2(p + thR[M] + 20), 1500, bits=1))
                l2.append({"job": 2, "M": int(M), "circuit": "W-ref", "role": "ref", "phi_deg": 0, "copy": cp, "part": "W"})
                c2.append(w_counts(0.9, 3000))
                l2.append({"job": 2, "M": int(M), "circuit": "Z", "role": "zero", "phi_deg": 0, "copy": cp, "m_clbit": 5, "part": "R"})
                c2.append(r_counts(0.01, 3000))
                l2.append({"job": 2, "M": int(M), "circuit": "P10", "role": "readout", "phi_deg": 0, "copy": cp, "m_clbit": 0, "part": "R"})
                c2.append(r_counts(ro[M][0], 1500, bits=1))
                l2.append({"job": 2, "M": int(M), "circuit": "P01", "role": "readout", "phi_deg": 0, "copy": cp, "m_clbit": 0, "part": "R"})
                c2.append(r_counts(1 - ro[M][1], 1500, bits=1))
        perm = rng.permutation(len(l2))                      # job 2 interleaved, as on the device
        l2, c2 = [l2[i] for i in perm], [c2[i] for i in perm]
        r = analyse(l1, c1, l2, c2, order, ps)
        rr = r["readout_measured"]
        ro_ok = all(abs(rr[M]["P1_given_0"] - ro[M][0]) < 0.02 and abs(rr[M]["P0_given_1"] - ro[M][1]) < 0.03 for M in order)
        good = r["H60"].startswith(name) and r["joint_generator_repeats_analyse_53"] and ro_ok
        ok = ok and good
        print(f"job 2 with the readout circuits, built to {name}: got {r['H60']} | phi* {ps} | informative {r['informative_cells']} | d1 "
              f"{ {c['M']: (round(c['d1'], 3), [round(x, 3) for x in c['d1_ci90']]) for c in r['cells_phi_star']} } | readout stated {ro} | measured "
              f"{ {M: (round(v['P1_given_0'], 3), round(v['P0_given_1'], 3)) for M, v in rr.items()} } | Z {r['zero_wait_baseline_any_above_0.1']} above 0.1 | "
              f"joint generator repeats analyse_53 {r['joint_generator_repeats_analyse_53']} | {'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'}")
    return ok
